symptom: Follow-up to ako/mxcli#1698: the upgrade property test failed on mdl-examples/bug-tests/action-slot-not-an-action-1062.fail.mdl — `container cCard (OnClick: TOTALLY_MADE_UP)` exec'd under mdl 0 and was refused under `mdl 1;` with MDL-WIDGET52 "`OnClick` is not a property mxcli writes on a container", although a container's OnClick IS its click action.
cause: The visitor stores `OnClick:` under "Action" only when the value parses as an action (#603); a malformed value falls through to the generic `key: value` branch and keeps its key AS WRITTEN. The per-widget verdict therefore saw an unknown `OnClick` key. Separately, MDL-WIDGET28 (the rule that owns a non-action value in an action slot) looked its slots up by exact key, so the same malformed value written `onClick:` — the casing the skills teach — or `action:` / `onchange:` was reported by nothing and written as a dead control.
file: mdl/executor/widget_native_props.go (nativeWidgetKeyAliases: onclick -> Action, used by nativeWidgetAccepts and the click-action ownership); mdl/executor/validate_widget_action_slot.go (actionSlotSpellings: every case on a built-in widget, exact on a pluggable one)
insight: A rule keyed on the AST's property names inherits every place the visitor renames a key conditionally: the well-formed value is under the new name, the malformed one under the old. Grep the visitor for dedicated branches that store under a different key than their token (here only ONCLICK -> "Action"; Visible/Editable lower to keys judged as a group, everything else keeps its name) and model each as an alias, not as a builder read. The sweep that missed it excluded .fail scripts — but the upgrade test executes a .fail script's mdl-0 original without check, so a gated refusal in a negative test is still a differential; sweep the .fail scripts too. Measured after: 0 MDL-WIDGET52 / MDL-V1-WIDGETPROP across all 1129 mdl-examples scripts other than the two intentional .fail tests (both already `mdl 1;`).
